day.text: Casey's Kookaburra can't learn Sphinx, so the claim about Drew doesn't fit. Drew's visit to Finley is confirmed by Blair and Finley's count. I'm backing the Casey throw.
day.note: Drew, Finley, Blair and Ellis now have consistent stories, while Casey's Sphinx claim on Drew contradicts Casey's own Kookaburra tool. I'll go with the table and throw at Casey, using a low card and keeping my Wink for later.
The table is converging on Casey and nothing new needs saying. I'll stay quiet and keep my Wink.

day.text: Casey's Kookaburra can't learn Sphinx, so the Drew claim is false and Casey is the throw. I'm calling it.
day.note: Consensus is forming on Casey, whose Sphinx claim can't come from a Kookaburra. I'll back the throw and push for an early vote.

day.text: Agreed, Casey is the throw. Calling CAW.
day.note: Table is converging on Casey, and I agree. Call CAW to push the vote.

day.text: Blair, Falcon, Farm. Casey's Sphinx claim is false, and the table agrees. I'm calling CAW CAW to move to the vote.
day.note: I'm Farm and the table agrees Casey's claim is false. Adding my caw to push the early vote, since Casey is the consensus throw.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: I'm Meowfia with a Mouser and a Wink. I'll visit Ellis to learn their role, since their Turkey claim is uncertain.

Blair.note: I'm Farm (Falcon). Drew's Kookaburra claim on me was false last round, so Drew is my top suspect. Visiting Drew shows who they visited.

Casey.note: I'm a Farm Kookaburra and want a role check. Drew's Kookaburra claim last round was called false, so I'll visit Drew to learn their role.

Drew.note: As Sphinx I know the farm roles are Falcon, Kookaburra, Owl and Turkey. Ellis's Turkey claim has been the most contested, so I'll visit the Turkey to see who it really is.

Ellis.note: Farm Owl again. No leads yet, so pick a player I haven't visited, Drew, to gather visitor info.

Alex.feeling: I'm the Mouser and know Ellis is the Owl, so I'm on the Farm-side read, though the table is about to eggsecute Casey on a shaky Sphinx claim.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 has been fairly clear: Casey's Sphinx claim broke on the table, but Alex's Mouser claim conflicts with their earlier Falcon claim, so I'm not sure about Alex.

Casey.feeling: Frustrating: my Kookaburra visit proved Drew is the Sphinx, but the table has turned on me and is about to throw at me, so I need the day vote to land on Drew.

Drew.feeling: The table is converging on Casey, which suits me, but Alex's Mouser claim and Casey's Sphinx accusation leave the round messy and hard to read.

Ellis.feeling: Casey's false Sphinx claim gave the table a clear target, but Drew's Tit visit and Blair's Falcon report still leave me unsure who is Meowfia.

Finley.feeling: Messy and tense: several role claims contradict each other, but Casey's Sphinx claim looks like the clearest lie so far.

Alex.note: The table has settled on Casey, so I'll throw at Casey with a low card, keeping my high cards.

Blair.note: I'm Farm and the table has settled on Casey. I'll throw my lowest card, H1, at Casey.

Casey.note: The table has turned on me, but Drew is the Sphinx per my own visit, so I'll throw at Drew with one cheap card to protect Farm's side.

Drew.note: Casey is Farm, so eggsecuting Casey gives Meowfia the round. Throwing my low H3 at Casey adds a vote and banks at full value if we win.

Ellis.note: Vote is called on Casey, whose Sphinx claim doesn't fit a Kookaburra. Throw one low card, S3, at Casey.

Finley.note: The table has agreed on Casey, and the Sphinx claim is false. I'll throw a Wild and a 6 at Casey to add votes while keeping my 8s and 9s and 12.

Alex.confusing: The Owl and Kookaburra dawn reports were hard to trust, since a visit sometimes didn't show up in the nest counts or the confusion flag. Turkey payouts also got tangled with Owl egg rules.
Alex.fun: Round 2 was fun to watch: the table caught Blair's Hawk claim by checking it against Ellis's flat count, and Blair retracted it.
Alex.change: I'd make dawn reports say explicitly who visited you and whether a visit paid out, so claims like Turkey or Owl egg rules are easier to check.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I threw my Wild at Casey, who was Farm, on a weak read, and Blair (the real Meowfia) went unchallenged. I'd have pushed harder on Blair's visit claims instead of following the table onto Casey.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were hard to track: I couldn't tell whether a visit to a Turkey paid the visitor, or whether the Owl's egg went to the Owl's own nest, so my round 2 claims got tangled.
Blair.fun: Round 1 was fun to watch: Casey's Kookaburra story unraveled as the table cross-checked egg counts and visits.
Blair.change: Publish each role's egg-gain rule in a single reference at the start of the game, so players don't have to reconstruct Turkey and Owl payouts from memory.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I claimed Hawk and visited Ellis while my own nest stayed flat, which contradicted the Turkey rule and got me eggsecuted. I should have stayed quiet or claimed a role whose report matched my flat count.

Casey.confusing: My Kookaburra dawn reports didn't show the role I learned from Blair in round 1, and they never flagged confusion even when someone visited me, so I couldn't tell whether my own information was valid.
Casey.fun: Round 2's Owl visit showed only a Hawk on Ellis, and the table's Hawk/Turkey claims and Blair's retraction turned into a real puzzle.
Casey.change: Show the learned role and any confusion explicitly in every dawn report, so players can check claims without guessing whether the report is wrong.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I revealed on day 1 that Drew was the Sphinx, which made the table defensive and turned their votes on me; I'd keep that quiet and throw at Drew with a bigger card instead.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were hard to track, since the table kept mixing up who pays whom. Confused reports also made it unclear whether a flat nest meant no visit or a wrong report.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was satisfying: as Meowfia Sphinx I had a verified Turkey read, and the table converged on Casey without my pushing. My Tit claim on Finley was believed.
Drew.change: I'd make the nest-change and egg-gain rules clearer, with a quick reminder of who pays whom for each role. The day would also move faster with fewer contradictory claims.
Drew.regret: In Round 1 I joined the throw on Casey, who was actually Farm, which handed the round to Meowfia. I should have pushed harder on Ellis's Owl story, since Ellis was the one whose claim didn't add up.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey rule was the hardest part: I first read it as the Turkey's own nest changing, then had to correct myself, and the table argued over whether a visit pays one egg or two. Also, the Owl's egg rule (paid to the Owl's own nest when no one else visited the target) was easy to misread as paying the target.
Ellis.fun: Round 2's Turkey and Hawk mix-up, where Finley claimed a Hawk hit on me and I had to correct my own Turkey mechanics in front of everyone, was a tense, funny bit of table debate.
Ellis.change: Put the Turkey and Owl payout rules in the dawn report or a short reminder so players don't have to reason them out from memory mid-day.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I threw at Blair and then pushed Casey in round 3 on a Sphinx argument, but I was often guessing rather than reading the egg counts. Next time I'd check each claim against the nest change before committing a card, and avoid spending a card on a throw I wasn't sure of.

Finley.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were easy to misread, and I got them wrong in day talk. Round 2's "Hawk" claims also looked identical because the Hawk only pays out on Meowfia, so flat and gained counts were easy to confuse.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was fun: Blair and Ellis's Turkey and Hawk claims collapsed under cross-checking, and we actually caught the lie in the open.
Finley.change: I'd make the dawn report state explicitly who paid an egg and why, so visitor-based egg changes are easier to verify.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I backed the Casey throw because I thought a Kookaburra couldn't have learned Sphinx, but Casey was Farm and Drew was the real Sphinx; I should have pushed Casey's Sphinx claim against Drew's own Tit story instead.

review.title: Casey Takes the Fall
review.headline: Farm eggsecuted its own Kookaburra twice, even after she named the Sphinx.
review.summary: Round 1 was a fog of misread Owl and Kookaburra rules, and Farm threw out Casey, who was Farm. Round 2 was the clean win: Blair's fake Hawk claim collapsed against her flat nest and the table hit the Floofer. In round 3 Casey truthfully outed Drew as the Sphinx, but the table decided a Kookaburra can't learn "Sphinx". They eggsecuted her and handed Meowfia the round. The game ended in a three-way tie at 10 between Alex, Casey and Drew.

rounds.recap: Blair (Floofer) hugged Ellis, and Alex and Casey were hugged too, so nobody gained or lost anything and no one had real evidence. The table argued over how the Owl egg works and fixated on Casey's missing Kookaburra report. Five players threw at Casey, who was Farm, and Blair won as the lone Meowfia.

Finley's Hawk egg and Casey's Owl report both pointed at Ellis, but Ellis was a Turkey who paid his visitors. Farm sorted that out after a few corrections. Blair then claimed Hawk, which clashed with Finley's real Hawk claim and with her own flat nest. She retracted it and the table eggsecuted her, a correct Farm win.

Casey, a Kookaburra, said she learned Drew was the Sphinx. Drew really was the Sphinx, but he claimed Tit, and Blair's Falcon report and his +1 egg both fit that story. The table argued that a Kookaburra learns a role and so can't see Sphinx. Three players called CAW and everyone but Casey and Drew's own throws went at Casey. Meowfia (Alex and Drew) won the round.

highlights.text: Blair claimed Hawk after Finley already had, her flat nest broke the lie, and Farm threw her out.
Casey told the plain truth that Drew was the Sphinx and was voted out for it.
Drew, the Sphinx, claimed Tit and used the egg from visiting the Turkey as proof, and the table bought it.
Alex, the Mouser, kept his Wink unused and quietly agreed with the Casey throw to win.

confusions.what: Said Casey should have gained an egg from the Owl visit. The Owl's egg goes to the Owl's own nest, and only if no one else visited.
Made the same Owl mistake and accused Ellis on it.
Claimed Hawk although Finley had already claimed it. Her flat nest also did not fit a Hawk visit to a Turkey.
Said Casey's Kookaburra should have been confused because of the Owl visit. Casey was hugged, which blocked the effect.
Argued Ellis could not be a Turkey because she gained only one egg. One visit to a Turkey pays exactly one egg, and her Owl egg did not land since Ellis was visited by others.
First said a flat nest meant nobody visited him. A Turkey's own nest never changes.
Read a flat nest as proof of no visitors, then corrected it. Also treated a Kookaburra's report as unable to name Sphinx, which it can (it learns the role).
Said a Kookaburra learns a role, not Sphinx. Sphinx is a role, so Casey's report was valid.
Treated Casey's Sphinx report as false and Drew's Tit claim as credible, though Drew's Tit claim could not be checked.
Argued Casey's Kookaburra cannot learn Sphinx, which is wrong. He is the Mouser and knew better.
Claimed her report showed no role for Blair. The visit was hugged, so she learned nothing, but she called it unreliable and then blamed the missing confusion.

worked: Round 2's Hawk, Owl and Turkey claims gave a real puzzle: egg counts could be cross-checked, and Blair's flat nest exposed her false Hawk claim.
The Sphinx and Kookaburra reports in round 3 gave Farm a true, usable lead, which makes the outcome a story about the table's reasoning, not luck.
Consolation returns, like Casey's S2, give a small reward for throwing at the right player even when the round is lost.
Meowfia not knowing each other led to real moves, like Blair's panic Hawk claim, and kept the cats from coordinating.
problems: Hugs blocking nearly everything in round 1 left the table with zero evidence, and nobody gained or lost an egg. The Floofer is too strong on a first night. Consider letting hugged visitors still report that they were hugged, or giving the Floofer a visible cost.

Role names are easy to misread. Several players said a Kookaburra "learns a role, not Sphinx", so the round-3 outcome rested on a rules misreading. Add a clear line that learning a role can show any animal, cats included.
Owl and Turkey egg rules caused repeated mistakes across all three rounds. Rewrite them with a worked example showing whose nest gains the egg.

Players followed the first plausible consensus and threw cheap Wilds, so the vote rarely tested anything. Throws of 0 or 1 card showed no confidence, and the 'Ties go to Meowfia' rule gave little reason to commit.
The Mouser's Wink was never used, and Alex held it all of round 3. With no downside to waiting it is too passive, so consider a timing limit or a cost.
